answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated results. A single operator can still create a dune of fake accounts, but each must tie up real capital; spreading the stake across a plume of identities does not reduce the total at risk. Audits sample work unpredictably, so a crystal-clear paper trail of repeated fraud can cost the attacker both locked funds and future access.
